fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. Abram travels through the land as far as the Oak of Moreh at Shechem. Then the text adds that the Canaanites were in the land. Other people are already living there, so Abram walks in as a newcomer and not as the only one on the block.

Not quite. The text says Terah lived 205 years, and he died in Haran (Genesis 11:32). Ur is where the family set out from, but the text says nothing about him going back there. I think this one is a heavy line, and the writer states it plainly.

That's right, baker! God says, “…go to the land I will show you.” The place isn't named yet, only the promise that God will show him. That takes real trust, friend. I'd have asked for directions twice and then packed extra cookie boxes.

That's it, friend! God says, “I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you…” A nation is a whole lot of people. That's like holding one lonely cookie and being told it will fill a stadium. Now that's a promise with some size to it.
